blocks.text: The Bukhara Biennial has announced the theme and the first round of confirmed artists for its upcoming edition, which takes place from 3 September to 21 November 2027.

Conceived and commissioned by Chairperson of Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation (ACDF), Gayane Umerova , the Bukhara Biennial’s second edition is guided by the notion of culture as infrastructure, with commissions planned to unfold across the city as both temporary and permanent works.

Under Artistic Director Kulapat Yantrasast , The Long Welcome draws on Bukhara’s history as a city on the Silk Road and a site of exchange. Building on the inaugural edition , the 2027 iteration will expand the collaboration between artists and local artisans to include ecologists, historians, teachers, musicians, and children, with all works created as new commissions and made exclusively in Uzbekistan.

Kulapat Yantrasast, Artistic Director of the Bukhara Biennial 2027, shared: “ The Long Welcome celebrates the spirit of hospitality that made Bukhara worth crossing continents to reach, and worth returning to again and again. When people welcome you into their city, you want to give something back. My hope is that an artist who returns to Bukhara years from now will find that something they made with people here has become part of everyday life.”

Anish Kapoor Koo Jeong A Sevara Haydarova Donazzan Susan Philipsz Nigina Mirzadzhanova Precious Okoyomon Ugo Rondinone Vivian Suter Joseph Arzoumanov Oscar Tuazon, Maksim Vardanyan and Daima Rakhmanbekova Huma Bhabha Bethan Laura Wood Bukhara Biennial 2027 runs from 3 September until 21 November 2027
